defects.source_claim: The source defines psi_k(i) as the suffix sum of y_j* from j=i through k-1 and prints the closed form 1-(1-1/k)^(k-i+1). The simple proof repeats the same shift by calling (k-i+1)/k precisely the unspent fraction of a type-i bidder whose exact spent fraction is i/k.
defects.source_locator: cited publication:713-731 and 777-819, Theorem 8 dual-suffix formula and simple-proof unspent coefficient
defects.status_impact_rationale: Summing the displayed geometric dual witness y_j*=(1/k)(1-1/k)^(k-j-1) from j=i through k-1 gives 1-(1-1/k)^(k-i), not exponent k-i+1. Likewise, exact spent fraction i/k leaves (k-i)/k unspent, not (k-i+1)/k. Both discrepancies are the same O(1/k) finite-index shift and do not change the k-to-infinity competitive-ratio conclusion. Lean proves both corrected identities and concrete k=2 refutations, so this is one minor corrected indexing note rather than a substantial paper caveat.

defects.status_impact_rationale: In the small-bids fluid limit, a tail bidder spends log(9/5) in phase 1 and 2/5 in phase 2, leaving the positive residual 3/5-log(9/5). The algorithm therefore serves positive phase-3 mass and has true normalized value 9/10-(1/2)log(9/5), rather than either printed 0.62 or the zero-phase-3 bookkeeping total 0.6. Lean proves the corrected execution feasible, proves its allocation-derived state updates and optimal offline value one, and proves the true factor remains strictly below 1-1/e. The intended qualitative conclusion is unchanged, so this is an ordinary formalized note, not a substantial caveat.
